openings.name: Ruy Lopez
openings.summary: Develop quickly, pressure the knight that defends e5, castle, and build the center with c3 and d4.
ideas: Bb5 attacks the knight that guards e5.
Castle early so the rook can support e4 from e1.
c3 prepares d4, and h3 keeps Black's bishop off g4.

mainLine.title: Claim the center
mainLine.explanation: The pawn controls d5 and f5 and opens lines for the queen and the light-squared bishop.

mainLine.title: Black matches you
mainLine.explanation: Black claims the same amount of central space.

mainLine.title: Develop with a threat
mainLine.explanation: The knight develops toward the center and attacks the pawn on e5.
mainLine.hint: Your g1 knight can attack e5 from f3.

mainLine.title: Black defends e5
mainLine.explanation: The knight defends e5 while developing.

mainLine.title: The Ruy Lopez
mainLine.explanation: The bishop puts pressure on the knight that defends e5. This is the move that defines the Ruy Lopez.
mainLine.hint: Put your light-squared bishop where it attacks the c6 knight.

mainLine.title: Morphy Defense
mainLine.explanation: Black asks the bishop where it wants to go. This is the most popular reply.

mainLine.title: Keep the pin
mainLine.explanation: Retreating to a4 keeps pressure on c6. Taking on c6 is fine too, but the main line keeps the bishop.
mainLine.hint: Keep the bishop on the same diagonal by stepping back one square.

mainLine.title: Black hits e4
mainLine.explanation: The knight develops and attacks your e4 pawn.

mainLine.title: Castle first
mainLine.explanation: Castling tucks your king away. If Black grabs e4, the rook can come to e1 and win the pawn back.
mainLine.hint: Get your king safe. Your kingside is clear.

mainLine.title: Black prepares to castle
mainLine.explanation: A calm developing move. The bishop makes room for Black to castle.

mainLine.title: Defend e4 with the rook
mainLine.explanation: The rook protects e4, so you are now really threatening to win e5 with Bxc6 and Nxe5.
mainLine.hint: Your f1 rook can defend e4 from the e-file.

mainLine.title: Black kicks the bishop
mainLine.explanation: Black gains space on the queenside and forces the bishop to move again.

mainLine.title: Aim at f7
mainLine.explanation: On b3 the bishop is safe and points at f7, Black's weakest square.
mainLine.hint: Move the bishop back to a safe square on the same diagonal as f7.

mainLine.title: Black supports e5
mainLine.explanation: The pawn protects e5 and opens the c8 bishop.

mainLine.title: Prepare d4
mainLine.explanation: c3 supports a later d4 and gives the bishop a retreat square on c2.
mainLine.hint: Play a quiet pawn move that prepares d4.

mainLine.title: Black castles
mainLine.explanation: Both kings are safe. The middlegame is about to begin.

mainLine.title: Stop ...Bg4
mainLine.explanation: h3 keeps Black's bishop off g4, where it would pin your knight. Now d4 comes next. This is the Closed Ruy Lopez.
mainLine.hint: Take g4 away from Black's light-squared bishop with a pawn move.

variations.name: Berlin Defense
variations.summary: Black ignores a6 and hits e4 straight away.

moves.title: What if 3...Nf6?
moves.explanation: The Berlin. Black develops and attacks e4 at once.

moves.title: Castle anyway
moves.explanation: You do not need to defend e4 yet. If Black takes it, you win time against the knight.
moves.hint: Calmly finish king safety. e4 can wait.

moves.title: Black takes the pawn
moves.explanation: Black grabs e4, but the king is still in the center.

moves.title: Open the center
moves.explanation: d4 attacks e5 and opens lines toward Black's uncastled king.
moves.hint: Strike the center with your d-pawn.

moves.title: The knight attacks the bishop
moves.explanation: The knight retreats and hits your bishop on b5.

moves.title: Trade on c6
moves.explanation: Capture the knight before Black chases the bishop away.
moves.hint: Take the knight that blocks Black's queenside.

moves.title: Black recaptures
moves.explanation: Black takes back toward the center and opens the d-file.

moves.title: Win space
moves.explanation: Capture on e5 and push the d6 knight away.
moves.hint: Capture the e5 pawn with a pawn.

moves.title: Knight to f5
moves.explanation: The knight finds a safe square. The queens are facing each other on the d-file.

moves.title: The Berlin endgame
moves.explanation: Trade queens with check. Black can no longer castle. This is the famous Berlin endgame.
moves.hint: The queens face each other on the d-file. Take with check.

variations.name: Classical Variation
variations.summary: Black develops the bishop to c5 and eyes f2.

moves.title: What if 3...Bc5?
moves.explanation: The Classical Defense. The bishop points at f2.

moves.title: Prepare d4
moves.explanation: c3 gets ready to hit the c5 bishop with d4 and gain time.
moves.hint: Prepare a central pawn break that will attack the c5 bishop.

moves.title: Black develops
moves.explanation: Black brings out the knight and gets ready to castle.

moves.title: Castle
moves.explanation: King safety first. Your rook may support e4 later.
moves.hint: Tuck your king away before opening the center.

moves.title: Black castles too
moves.explanation: Both kings are safe.

moves.title: Strike the center
moves.explanation: d4 attacks the bishop and the e5 pawn. That was the point of c3.
moves.hint: Now play the move c3 prepared.

variations.name: Schliemann Defense
variations.summary: Black counterattacks with an early f5.

moves.title: What if 3...f5?
moves.explanation: The Schliemann. A sharp gambit that attacks e4 and opens the f-file.

moves.title: Defend and develop
moves.explanation: The knight protects e4 and develops. It is the most solid reply.
moves.hint: Develop a piece that also defends e4.

moves.title: Black takes
moves.explanation: Black captures on e4 and the knight is attacked.

moves.title: Recapture
moves.explanation: Take back with the knight. It stands well in the center.
moves.hint: Win the pawn back with the piece that defended it.

moves.title: Black hits the knight
moves.explanation: Black attacks the e4 knight, but leaves e5 weak.

moves.title: Counterattack
moves.explanation: Ignore the threat and take e5. Your knight hits c6, and Black's pieces are loose.
moves.hint: Your f3 knight can capture a central pawn.

variations.name: Modern Steinitz Defense
variations.summary: After 3...a6 4.Ba4, Black plays a solid d6 instead of Nf6.

moves.title: What if 4...d6?
moves.explanation: The Modern Steinitz. Black supports e5 and keeps the position closed.

moves.title: Build the center
moves.explanation: c3 prepares d4 and keeps a retreat for the bishop.
moves.hint: Prepare d4 with a quiet pawn move.

moves.title: Black unpins
moves.explanation: The bishop guards c6 so the knight is no longer pinned.

moves.title: Take the center
moves.explanation: With c3 played, d4 builds a big pawn center.
moves.hint: Now push the pawn that c3 supports.

variations.ecoName: Ruy Lopez: Morphy Defense, Modern Steinitz Defense

variations.name: Open Variation
variations.summary: After 5.O-O, Black grabs the e4 pawn.

moves.title: What if 5...Nxe4?
moves.explanation: The Open Variation. Black wins a pawn but opens the position while the king is still in the center.

moves.title: Hit the center
moves.explanation: d4 opens lines and gets ready to win the pawn back.
moves.hint: Break with the d-pawn, just as in the Berlin.

moves.title: Black kicks the bishop
moves.explanation: Black gains time on the a4 bishop.

moves.title: Bishop to b3
moves.explanation: The bishop stays active, pointing at d5 and f7.
moves.hint: Retreat the bishop to the diagonal that aims at f7.

moves.title: Black supports the knight
moves.explanation: d5 holds the knight on e4.

moves.title: Win the pawn back
moves.explanation: Material is equal again, and your e5 pawn gains space.
moves.hint: Capture on e5 with a pawn.

moves.title: Black protects d5
moves.explanation: The bishop defends d5.

moves.title: A home for the bishop
moves.explanation: c3 gives the b3 bishop a safe square on c2 and supports later play.
moves.hint: Make a quiet pawn move that gives your bishop a retreat.

variations.name: Marshall Attack
variations.summary: Black castles early and sacrifices a pawn with ...d5.

moves.title: What if 7...O-O?
moves.explanation: Black castles before d6. Watch out for the Marshall Attack.

moves.title: Prepare d4
moves.explanation: The same plan as the main line: c3 first.
moves.hint: Play the same quiet pawn move as in the main line.

moves.title: The Marshall gambit
moves.explanation: Black gives up a pawn to open lines toward your king.

moves.title: Accept the pawn
moves.explanation: Take the pawn. Defending is part of learning this line.
moves.hint: Capture the d5 pawn.

moves.title: Black recaptures
moves.explanation: The knight jumps to d5 and e5 is left without a pawn defender.

moves.title: Win a pawn
moves.explanation: Take e5. You are a pawn up, but Black gets active pieces.
moves.hint: Your f3 knight can capture a central pawn.

moves.title: Black trades knights
moves.explanation: Black removes your active knight.

moves.title: The rook recaptures
moves.explanation: The rook takes back on e5.
moves.hint: Recapture with the piece on the e-file.

moves.title: Black supports d5
moves.explanation: Black protects the knight and prepares Bd6 to attack your rook.

moves.title: Develop the queenside
moves.explanation: d4 opens the c1 bishop and controls e5. Bring pieces out before Black's attack arrives.
moves.hint: Push the d-pawn to free your dark-squared bishop.

openings.name: Caro-Kann Defense
openings.summary: Prepare d5 with c6, keep your structure solid, and develop the light-squared bishop before e6.
ideas: c6 supports d5 without blocking your light-squared bishop.
Get the bishop out to f5 or g4 before you play e6.
Against h-pawn pushes, answer calmly with h6 and keep the bishop safe.

mainLine.title: White claims the center
mainLine.explanation: White takes central space.

mainLine.title: The Caro-Kann
mainLine.explanation: c6 prepares d5 and keeps the c8 bishop free.
mainLine.hint: Push the c-pawn one square to support d5 next.

mainLine.title: White builds the center
mainLine.explanation: White adds a second central pawn.

mainLine.title: Challenge e4
mainLine.explanation: d5 attacks the e4 pawn. c6 means you can recapture with a pawn.
mainLine.hint: Strike at e4 with your d-pawn.

mainLine.title: White defends e4
mainLine.explanation: The knight develops and protects e4.

mainLine.title: Take on e4
mainLine.explanation: Capture the pawn. The knight will recapture.

mainLine.title: White recaptures
mainLine.explanation: The knight sits in the center.

mainLine.title: The Classical move
mainLine.explanation: Develop the bishop with tempo on the knight before you play e6.
mainLine.hint: Bring out the light-squared bishop and attack the e4 knight.

mainLine.title: White attacks the bishop
mainLine.explanation: The knight retreats and hits f5.

mainLine.title: Keep the bishop
mainLine.explanation: The bishop stays on its good diagonal.
mainLine.hint: Step back along the diagonal to stay safe.

mainLine.title: White threatens h5
mainLine.explanation: White wants to trap the bishop with h5.

mainLine.title: Make an escape square
mainLine.explanation: h6 gives the bishop a home on h7.
mainLine.hint: Give your bishop an escape square with a pawn move.

mainLine.title: White develops
mainLine.explanation: The knight develops toward the center.

mainLine.title: Guard e5
mainLine.explanation: The knight stops Ne5 and prepares Ngf6.
mainLine.hint: Develop the b8 knight so it controls e5.

mainLine.title: White pushes on
mainLine.explanation: White hits the bishop again.

mainLine.title: Use the escape square
mainLine.explanation: That is why you played h6.
mainLine.hint: Retreat to the square h6 prepared.

mainLine.title: White offers a trade
mainLine.explanation: White challenges your strong bishop.

mainLine.title: Trade bishops
mainLine.explanation: Take the bishop. White recaptures with the queen.
mainLine.hint: Capture the piece that challenges your bishop.

mainLine.title: White recaptures
mainLine.explanation: The queen takes back and eyes the kingside.

mainLine.title: Solid and ready
mainLine.explanation: Now that the bishop is gone, e6 is safe. Next come Ngf6, Be7, and castling.
mainLine.hint: Open your dark-squared bishop with a central pawn move.

variations.name: Two Knights Attack
variations.summary: White develops a knight instead of playing d4.

moves.title: What if 2.Nc3?
moves.explanation: White delays d4 and develops.

moves.title: Stick to the plan
moves.explanation: d5 still challenges e4.
moves.hint: Play the central pawn move that c6 prepared.

moves.title: White develops again
moves.explanation: The second knight comes out.

moves.title: Pin the knight
moves.explanation: The bishop pins the knight to the queen before you play e6.
moves.hint: Develop the light-squared bishop with a pin.

variations.name: Advance Variation
variations.summary: White pushes past d5 with e5.

moves.title: What if 3.e5?
moves.explanation: The Advance Variation. White gains space and blocks the center.

moves.title: Bishop out first
moves.explanation: Develop the bishop before e6 locks it in.
moves.hint: Bring the light-squared bishop out before closing it in.

moves.title: White develops
moves.explanation: White develops calmly.

moves.title: Now e6
moves.explanation: The bishop is already outside the pawn chain.
moves.hint: With the bishop out, support d5 with your e-pawn.

moves.title: White prepares to castle
moves.explanation: White gets ready to castle.

moves.title: Hit the chain
moves.explanation: c5 attacks the base of White's pawn chain on d4.
moves.hint: Attack d4 with a pawn.

moves.title: What if 3.exd5?
moves.explanation: The Exchange Variation. White releases the tension.

moves.title: Recapture with the c-pawn
moves.explanation: Taking back with the c-pawn keeps a pawn in the center.
moves.hint: Recapture toward the center.

moves.title: White eyes h7
moves.explanation: The bishop points at your kingside.

moves.title: Develop
moves.explanation: The knight develops and pressures d4.
moves.hint: Develop a knight that pressures d4.

moves.title: White supports d4
moves.explanation: White protects d4.

moves.title: Develop again
moves.explanation: The second knight comes out and guards h7.
moves.hint: Develop the other knight.

moves.title: White develops
moves.explanation: The bishop takes the b8-h2 diagonal.

moves.title: Active bishop
moves.explanation: The bishop attacks the queen on d1 and gets outside the pawn chain.
moves.hint: Develop your light-squared bishop with an attack on the queen.

variations.name: Panov Attack
variations.summary: After the exchange, White plays c4 to attack d5.

moves.title: What if 3.exd5 and 4.c4?
moves.explanation: White trades on d5, planning c4.

moves.title: Recapture
moves.explanation: Same recapture as in the Exchange.
moves.hint: Recapture toward the center.

moves.title: The Panov Attack
moves.explanation: White attacks d5 again and aims for open lines.

moves.title: Defend d5
moves.explanation: The knight develops and defends d5.
moves.hint: Defend d5 with a developing move.

moves.title: More pressure
moves.explanation: White adds another attacker on d5.

moves.title: Hold d5
moves.explanation: e6 gives d5 solid support and opens your bishop.
moves.hint: Support d5 with a pawn.

openings.ecoName: Caro-Kann Defense: Classical Variation, Spassky Variation
